text:
# Mailloop

Personalized job outreach from your own Gmail. Production domain: **https://mailloop.in**.

Create templates, import contacts, preview emails for up to 10 recipients, attach a resume, track submissions, and mark replies manually. Every message has one recipient; Mailloop never batches through CC or BCC.

| Plan    | Recipients per campaign | Emails per UTC day | Emails per month |
| ------- | ----------------------: | -----------------: | ---------------: |
| Free    |                       3 |                  3 |               15 |
| Premium |                      10 |                 20 |              300 |

Daily allowances include sent and queued emails and reset at midnight UTC. Free monthly allowances follow the UTC calendar month; Premium follows the verified subscription billing period. When plan gating is disabled, the legacy allowance remains 200 emails per rolling 24 hours.

## Run locally

Requirements: Node.js 24 LTS, npm 11.19.0 (matching CI), Docker Compose, and a Google OAuth web client with Gmail API enabled.

1. Keep your existing `.env`, or copy `.env.example` to `.env` for a fresh checkout. For a new database, generate a local password with `openssl rand -hex 32`, set `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, and use the same password in `DATABASE_URL`. Fill in the remaining secrets; never commit `.env`.
2. Run `npm ci` (generates Prisma Client).
3. Run `docker compose up -d postgres`.
4. Run `npm run db:deploy` to apply checked-in migrations. No database reset is needed.
5. Run `npm run dev` on the host at **http://localhost:3000**.
6. In a second terminal, run `npm run inngest:dev`. Keep `INNGEST_DEV=1` locally so events go to the local Inngest dev server.
7. Sign in, save a template and contacts, optionally upload a PDF in Settings, and send from Compose.

Docker runs PostgreSQL only. The database is bound to **127.0.0.1:5433** to avoid the existing host listener at 5432 and restrict access to the local host. `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` must be set; Compose has no password fallback. The `mailloop_postgres_data` volume is preserved. Do not run `docker compose down -v` unless you intend to erase the database.

On an existing database, changing `.env` does not rotate the password stored in the volume. Rotate it through PostgreSQL's `\password mailloop` command in an authenticated administrative session, then update `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `DATABASE_URL` to match. Recreate the PostgreSQL service with `docker compose up -d postgres` to apply the loopback binding without removing the volume.

The original scaffold, schema, generated-client path, and initial migration are retained. Prisma's configuration is now named `prisma.config.ts`. All three Prisma packages are pinned to **7.10.0**; do not upgrade them or use `prisma db push` to bypass migration history.

## Clear local test data

Stop Next.js, Inngest and subscription maintenance processes, then run:

```sh
npm run db:clear                 # Preview the reset; all changes roll back
npm run db:clear -- --apply      # Clear local app records
```

This deletes all local accounts, contacts, templates, attachments metadata,
campaigns, history, usage, billing records, deletion jobs and audit records.
It preserves the schema, migrations and the entire `SystemControl` record,
including plan limits, checkout enablement and Dodo test business binding.
Missing system settings cause the reset to fail rather than invent defaults.
The command accepts only the configured local Docker database on port 5433 and
rejects production mode. Restart the app and workers and sign in again afterward.
External Gmail messages, Blob files and Dodo test subscriptions are unaffected;
finish or cancel provider test subscriptions before clearing their local records.
Use this command instead of truncating every table or `prisma migrate reset`.

## Environment

| Variable                                            | Purpose                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DATABASE_URL`                                      | Local: `postgresql://mailloop:<your-password>@127.0.0.1:5433/mailloop`; production: managed PostgreSQL URL |
| `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `POSTGRES_DB` | Local Docker database configuration                                                                        |
| `AUTH_URL`                                          | `http://localhost:3000` locally; **`https://mailloop.in`** in production                                   |
| `AUTH_SECRET`                                       | Auth.js session encryption secret; generate with `openssl rand -base64 32`                                 |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`          | Google OAuth web client credentials                                                                        |
| `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`                              | Separate 32-byte AES-GCM key, encoded as 64 hexadecimal characters                                         |
| `INNGEST_DEV`                                       | `1` for local development only; unset in production                                                        |
| `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY`, `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY`          | Production Inngest event publishing and callback signature verification                                    |
| `BLOB_STORE_ID`, `BLOB_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_KEY`          | Provided by a **private** Vercel Blob store using OIDC in production                                       |
| `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`                             | Alternative credential for legacy private Blob stores                                                      |

Generate the token encryption key once:

```sh
node -e "console.log(require('node:crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"
```

Keep this key backed up securely. Changing it makes existing refresh tokens unreadable; key rotation requires decrypting/re-encrypting existing tokens or reconnecting every account. It is independent of `AUTH_SECRET`.

Secrets are never sent as client props or returned by actions. Logs and Inngest events/step outputs contain no OAuth tokens, email bodies, or raw MIME messages.

## Google OAuth

Enable Gmail API and configure a **Web application** OAuth client. Add these exact authorized redirect URIs:

- Local: `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google`
- Production: **`https://mailloop.in/api/auth/callback/google`**

Use `http://localhost:3000` and `https://mailloop.in` as the corresponding origins. Configure the consent screen and add your Gmail account as a test user during development. Request `openid`, `email`, `profile`, `gmail.send`.

Mailloop requests offline access and consent. Google returns a refresh token, which is encrypted before storing it. If a later login omits the token, the saved token remains intact. Settings offers reconnection for revoked/expired permission. Do not automatically link existing users based only on matching email addresses; users are bound to Google's stable account ID.

Mailloop requests sending permission only and never reads Gmail. Existing broad tokens cannot enable reads. Reconnecting does not revoke old grants: remove Mailloop in Google Manage Access and reconnect if broader permissions remain.

Sources: [Auth.js Google provider](https://authjs.dev/reference/core/providers/google), [Google Gmail scopes](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/auth/scopes), [Google OAuth token expiration](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2#expiration).

## Features and behavior

- **Templates:** Plain-text name, subject, and body, with a reference example and cursor insertion buttons. Supported placeholders are `{{name}}`, `{{company}}`, and `{{role}}`. Unknown/incomplete placeholders are rejected. Missing company values become empty text; every recipient needs a job role. Paste your portfolio, GitHub, LinkedIn, or other links directly into the message. You can include multiple links. Use full HTTP/HTTPS URLs to make them clickable. Delivery includes HTML and plain-text alternatives. The HTML uses natural width, left-aligned email typography, and preserves authored line breaks; typed HTML is escaped. Messages support `**bold**`, bullet lines starting with `- ` or `* `, and numbered lists starting with `1. `; these formats also appear in the live previews. The plain-text alternative keeps the authored symbols. Both template and Compose previews show the complete personalized message in a keyboard-accessible scrolling area capped at `min(440px, 55dvh)`, with controls, subject, and validation outside it. The message editor starts at `min(360px, 45dvh)` and can be resized vertically. Existing templates need no migration, and previously delivered messages remain unchanged. The complete example includes sample links and a signature to replace; attach the resume in Compose or remove the attachment sentence.
- **Contacts:** Both plans can save any job role without a custom-role quota. Settings supports up to 2 saved role shortcuts on Free or 8 on Premium, using any role text. Contacts shows only saved shortcuts, with no defaults when none are saved. Existing shortcuts above the limit can be retained or removed; adding or replacing requires fitting the current limit. Only Premium can override individual recipient roles in Compose; the preview updates automatically and saved contacts stay unchanged. Free uses the contact’s saved role, with server-side enforcement. Contacts require an editable name, email, and job role; company is optional. Email-derived names are suggestions and generic addresses need correction. Import comma/semicolon/newline email lists, CSV/TSV, or a CSV file with an `email` header. Optional columns are `name`, `company`, and `jobRole` (or `role`). Imports accept up to 1,000 rows / 1 MB, support quoted CSV, and provide editable, paginated previews and a bulk role selector. Correct unresolved names and roles before saving; duplicates are skipped. Emails are trimmed and lowercased; Gmail dot/plus aliases are not collapsed. Legacy Tag/Notes data remains in the database, and roles are backfilled from the latest nonempty campaign role when available.
- **Compose:** Select up to 3 recipients on Free or 10 on Premium and one template. Each recipient starts with their contact's job role, with batch-only overrides, saved shortcuts, filtering, and Apply Role to Selected. Preview each recipient separately. Contacts already sent/replied show local Last Sent timestamps and are skipped unless explicitly selected for resending. Queued and uncertain deliveries cannot be overridden.
- **Links and resume attachment:** Paste URLs directly into templates. Upload a resume PDF (up to 5 MiB) in Settings, then select “Attach Resume” in Compose; attachment defaults off. Mentioning a PDF in the message does not attach it. Both MIME type and PDF header are checked. Local uploads are stored under ignored `uploads/`; production uses private Blob with authenticated direct uploads, avoiding Vercel's function request-body limit. The server validates the uploaded file before activating it. Only the authenticated owner's current resume can be downloaded. Queued messages retain the chosen PDF and complete rendered message after later edits. Migration `20261008020000_inline_template_links` replaces every body `{{link}}` occurrence (including whitespace variants and archived templates) with the owner’s saved URL, then removes the saved-link column. Where no URL exists, the placeholder stays visible and preview/sending report “Replace {{link}} with a URL directly in your message.” Queued and historical snapshots remain unchanged.
- **History:** Sends redirect to `History?campaign=<id>` with queued, sent, failed, cancelled, and delivery-review counts. Progress refreshes every 5 seconds while visible and active. Approximate remaining ranges include all outstanding sends for that user and the persisted next-send delay; service delays can extend them. Completion comes from delivery states rather than a countdown. Recipient/company/role/template snapshots, filters, pagination, and automatic refresh are preserved. Sent Today uses a UTC calendar day; the quota uses the rolling last 24 hours.
- **Appearance:** Geist typography, restrained blue accents, matching light/dark tokens, and locally remembered Light/Dark/System choices. System is the default; the theme is applied before first paint. Explicit switches use brief opacity transitions and respect reduced motion. The account avatar menu contains account details, Settings, and Sign Out with keyboard and outside-click support.
- **Manual replies:** History offers Mark replied for sent messages and Undo for replied messages, including existing REPLIED rows. Both are available to all users. Marking a reply stops matching reminders; Undo restores eligibility. Mailloop does not read the inbox or detect replies. Add to shortlist prepares a follow-up for review in Compose. SENT means Gmail accepted submission, not confirmed recipient delivery. Legacy bounce records remain stored/exportable but have no effect on eligibility and are not displayed.
- **History deletion:** Settings permanently deletes eligible completed `Send` rows and reminders in a user-locked transaction. Successful sends become minimal `DeliveryReceipt` rows containing only a UUID, user ID, recipient address, original creation time, and successful-send time. Receipts remain until account deletion; quotas and yellow address warnings include both live sends and receipts. Queued, attempting, and uncertain sends remain. Empty campaigns retain idempotency keys while role and attachment references are cleared. Gmail emails remain unchanged.
- **Quota:** Up to 200 emails per rolling 24 hours, counting accepted submissions plus outstanding queue reservations and recent uncertain attempts. Capacity returns automatically as successful sends and uncertain attempts reach 24 hours old; READY queues and actively ATTEMPTING work remain reserved. The workspace refreshes usage every 60 seconds while visible and on return to the tab. Mailloop cannot reserve quota for emails you send outside the app; Gmail may impose additional account limits.
- **Cancellation:** Cancellation remains supported by the server for account deletion; History no longer displays cancellation buttons. The user-row lock serializes cancellation with delivery claims. Sent, actively sending, and uncertain messages cannot be stopped. Cancelled sends release quota reservations, finish campaign progress without claiming successful delivery, and release superseded PDFs once no remaining send needs them.
- **Export and account deletion:** Settings downloads a private, uncached JSON export from `/api/account/export`; credentials and storage locations are excluded. Typed-email confirmation disables access, cancels ready sends, and attempts billing cancellation immediately. The request is irreversible. The daily deletion sweep at 02:00 UTC / 07:30 IST processes requests after a minimum 15-minute drain, removing ordinary content and owned PDFs independently of billing/provider outages. Unfinished stages retry in later daily runs, with a 30-day target from the original request. A minimal recovery job and keyed Google identity hash prevent reactivation while deletion is pending. Retained revocation credentials are erased one daily interval before their original deadline. Signed Blob completion callbacks retain their separate drain protection and remove late uploads for disabled or missing accounts. Deleting Mailloop does not delete Gmail or recipient copies.
- **Follow-up reminders:** Default to 7 days; Settings also offers Off, 3, or 14 days. History computes a paginated due list on each load using the latest successful send, matching contact IDs and immutable recipient addresses. Replies, pending/uncertain deliveries, archived contacts, and an existing shortlist request suppress reminders. Rows use “No reply marked”; users record replies manually. Use Add to shortlist in History to prepare a follow-up; Compose is always the approval step.
- **Public policies:** `/privacy` and `/terms` are public and linked at sign-in, the landing footer, and Settings. The operator is Czar16; support is `[REDACTED_EMAIL]`. Review their wording and actual production provider/retention practices before launch.
- **Contact/template removal:** Contacts/templates are archived so queued emails and history survive. Resume replacement/removal affects new campaigns; queued messages retain their original version. Superseded files are deleted only when no queued/uncertain send requires them.

## How sending works

`src/lib/campaigns.ts` locks the user row in a short transaction, revalidates ownership/duplicates/quota, and snapshots each rendered message, recipient, template name, and attachment. An idempotency key makes repeated submission of the same campaign return its original result.

Each `Send` row acts as a durable outbox entry. `src/lib/inngest.ts` publishes one event per recipient using only `userId` and `sendId`. Campaign submission dispatches immediately; `quota-reconciliation` retries pending publishing and repairs accounting hourly (`0 * * * *`, UTC). Interrupted dispatches and deferred sends may wait up to one hour after becoming eligible. Event IDs and database delivery state protect against duplicate execution.

Daily maintenance (`0 3 * * *`, 03:00 UTC / 08:30 IST) uses one discovery step to paginate accounts and publishes per-account cleanup events in batches of 100 only for active accounts with unused attachments awaiting physical deletion. Idle accounts produce no cleanup events. Attachment cleanup processes at most ten files in a batch, preserves current attachments and those needed by queued, attempting, or uncertain sends, and records successful physical deletion while retaining historical metadata. Backlogs continue on later daily passes, so newly eligible cleanup may wait up to one day. Failed deletions remain pending for retry; local files already absent count as completed. Apply migration `20261013000000_attachment_storage_cleanup` and regenerate Prisma Client before running this version.

With no pending work, the current Inngest schedules use at least 56 executions/day (1,680 per 30 days): quota reconciliation hourly, daily deletion discovery (three steps), daily attachment maintenance, and daily rate-limit cleanup. Operator monitoring, alert delivery, and the 15-minute deletion-maintenance job are removed. Sending, additional pages, cleanup events/workers, pacing, and retries consume additional executions; previously consumed quota is unchanged.

The worker serializes active delivery steps per user. It checks `nextSendAt` in the database and uses `step.sleepUntil` instead of blocking a request. Sends are normally spaced about 5 seconds apart; Gmail limits may extend waits. The first send starts immediately if no persisted account wait exists. After each completed attempt the worker persists the shared `NORMAL_SEND_INTERVAL_SECONDS` delay (initially 5); separate campaigns share the same pacing. Existing persisted waits are retained, and the 60-second crash reservation remains. Inngest concurrency alone would not suffice because sleeping releases the execution slot.

`src/lib/gmail.ts` builds UTF-8 MIME with exactly one `To` address and an optional PDF, then sends the base64url-encoded message through Gmail API. The maintained MIME composer is installed as `gmail-mime`, separating it from Auth.js's unused optional Nodemailer provider dependency.

Delivery is **not exactly once** across Gmail and PostgreSQL. Ambiguous timeout/crash outcomes become FAILED/UNCERTAIN and immediately stop automatic processing. Check Gmail Sent yourself. History displays the uncertainty without a confirmation or resend button. Uncertain sends remain Needs review. Its quota consumption expires after 24 hours, but duplicate blocking persists. Each email gets one sending attempt, and the email worker has automatic retries disabled. Preparation failures and definite Gmail rejections finish without another automatic attempt and release reserved capacity. Rate-limit rejections retain account/project cooldowns for other queued messages. Legacy queued retries are finalized without another send.

Trade-offs: JWT sessions avoid additional Auth.js session tables; plain-text templates avoid a rich-text editor; private Blob avoids public URLs and ephemeral production disk; the MIME library handles Unicode and multipart encoding rather than handwritten MIME; authenticated routes use request-time rendering rather than caching user-specific data.

## Verify

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm test
npm run test:db
npm run test:e2e
npm run build
npx prisma migrate status
```

`npm run test:usage:db` creates a disposable Docker PostgreSQL database, applies migrations, runs usage and database tests, and removes only that test container and its storage. Use it to verify background-job changes without touching the development database.

Database/browser tests require the **local** database with checked-in migrations. Tests create and delete only UUID-scoped fixtures. Gmail calls are mocked in database tests. Browser tests use a separate server on port 3100, signed test-session cookies, fake refresh tokens, and an unreachable Inngest event endpoint; they never send real emails. Test artifacts are ignored.

Browser checks run desktop Chrome and mobile emulation with axe accessibility scans. Set `CHROME_PATH` when needed, or install Playwright's browser with `npx playwright install chromium`.

For a real smoke test, sign in with a user-controlled Google test account and send to another address you control. Verify the PDF, Gmail Sent message, manual reply marking and follow-up shortlisting, and reconnection. Real OAuth consent, Gmail delivery, and production Blob need valid external configuration and are not simulated by passing automated tests.

## Deploy to Vercel

Dodo subscription settlement rules, isolated verification, webhook setup and
deletion safeguards are documented in [Dodo test billing](docs/dodo-test-billing.md).
For production setup, use the [live billing rollout](docs/dodo-live-rollout.md).

1. Connect this repository and configure a managed PostgreSQL database. Keep local Docker out of production.
2. Set production environment variables, including **`AUTH_URL=https://mailloop.in`**, separate secrets, and a **private** Blob store token. Do not set `INNGEST_DEV` in production.
3. Back up the production database, then run `npm run db:deploy` against the production database as a controlled release step, then build with `npm run build`. Prisma Client is generated during installation; retain dev dependencies for the build/migration stage.
4. Connect Inngest to **`https://mailloop.in/api/inngest`** and configure the event/signing keys. Synchronize the registered functions. Verify `quota-reconciliation` uses `0 * * * *`, `maintenance` uses `0 3 * * *`, and `rate-limit-cleanup` uses `0 4 * * *` (UTC). Confirm `minimum-hardening-monitor`, `operator-alert-delivery`, `scheduled-replies`, and `refresh-replies` are absent. Auth.js entrypoints and service callbacks use provider verification; all user actions remain session-authenticated and user-scoped.
5. Add **mailloop.in** in Vercel Domains and configure the DNS records shown by Vercel. Complete Google production consent configuration using the callback above.
6. Review the public policies and confirm production hosting, PostgreSQL, private Blob, Inngest, and backup-retention practices. Configure Google consent with `https://mailloop.in/`, `https://mailloop.in/privacy`, `https://mailloop.in/terms`, and the production callback. Complete applicable Google OAuth verification/security assessment requirements for the requested Gmail scope before broad launch.
7. Verify sign-in, a controlled individual email with a PDF, private PDF access, signature-protected Inngest callbacks, manual reply marking and follow-up shortlisting, cancellation, export, reconnection, and deletion with accounts you control. Verify backups and monitor disabled accounts awaiting cleanup as well as failed sends, uncertain deliveries, and pending dispatch before inviting beta users. Do not log message contents or credentials.

The root layout includes Vercel Web Analytics, Speed Insights, and Google Analytics web stream `G-JMR4H98NTK`. Enable Web Analytics and Speed Insights in the Vercel project dashboard, then deploy and visit the site to begin collecting data. Google Analytics uses the stream's measurement ID directly; do not also publish a GA4 pageview tag for this stream through Google Tag Manager, as that would duplicate pageviews. Public URLs are listed in `/sitemap.xml`, with private app routes excluded from `/robots.txt` and marked `noindex` in their layouts.

Useful references: [Private Blob](https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage), [Blob client uploads](https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload), [Inngest concurrency](https://www.inngest.com/docs/durable-execution/flow-control/concurrency).

## Dependency audit

Prisma remains exactly 7.10.0 as required. The current `npm audit --omit=dev` reports four high-severity findings in Prisma CLI tooling and its `@prisma/config`, `deepmerge-ts`, and `mysql2` dependencies. The app uses PostgreSQL through `@prisma/adapter-pg`; it does not use the MySQL driver or accept user-provided Prisma configuration. Keep the CLI in the build/migration environment and track the upstream advisories. Do not run `npm audit fix --force`, which proposes changing the required Prisma version.

## Launch migration and cleanup operations

Keep full email history for launch and review database storage weekly using the [storage monitoring runbook](docs/storage-monitoring.md) and [read-only SQL report](ops/storage-report.sql). Review retention at 70% of the production plan's actual storage allowance, or when measured growth projects reaching that threshold within 30 days. This triggers review only; automatic retention is not enabled.

`20261010010000_launch_controls` adds `SendStatus.CANCELLED`, `Send.cancelledAt`, `User.deletionRequestedAt`, and `User.followUpDays` (default 7, constrained to 0/3/7/14). It is additive and preserves existing send history. Keep Prisma at 7.10.0 and apply migrations before deploying the new queries.

Register the updated Inngest functions after deployment. `account-deletion-jobs` runs daily at 02:00 UTC (`0 2 * * *`); remove the old `deletion-maintenance` registration. Billing cancellation is attempted inline when deletion is requested; daily workers retry unfinished stages. `maintenance` handles only active-account attachment cleanup at 03:00 UTC (`0 3 * * *`). A deletion request remains durable if Inngest is temporarily unavailable. Investigate unfinished jobs approaching their original 30-day target. Provider-managed backup/log retention must be established with the actual providers. Automated tests use mocked providers; production Blob cleanup and real OAuth still need controlled live checks.

`20261012000000_permanent_history` adds delivery receipts, backfills eligible soft-deleted successful history, and physically removes eligible soft-deleted sends atomically. Apply it before deploying the new queries. `historyDeletedAt` remains for compatibility with unresolved legacy rows. Selecting a yellow recipient in Compose authorizes their follow-up; deselecting removes authorization. Bulk selection continues to exclude previously emailed recipients.

Queue estimates are approximate: existing account wait + remaining 5-second gaps + a 5-second processing allowance per outstanding email. For 10 recipients, gaps total 45 seconds and the initial estimate is 95 seconds without an existing wait. Service latency can extend it; an expired timer shows “Sending” while work remains. “Sent” means Gmail accepted the send, not that it arrived in the recipient’s inbox.

Before general rollout, run a small campaign to controlled recipient addresses and review completion time, throttling, and uncertain outcomes without logging tokens or email bodies. If throttling increases, raise `NORMAL_SEND_INTERVAL_SECONDS` to 10.

Send-only deployment: apply `20261016000000_send_only_v1` and regenerate the pinned Prisma 7.10.0 client. Stop old workers before deploying. Synchronize Inngest and verify that `scheduled-replies` and `refresh-replies` are absent. Apply `20261016020000_remove_recipient_suppression` to remove unused suppression storage. Preserve applied migration history. Roll back cleanup or UI changes independently while retaining send-only OAuth, disabled reads, and uncertain-send protections. Test only against disposable local databases; verify real OAuth and individual sending with accounts you control.

Subscription deadlines use fresh checks at dispatch and claim. The production
Inngest app runs queued campaign cleanup and billing recovery every four hours,
and reconciliation daily. Billing webhooks process receipts directly;
monitor these [billing schedules](docs/dodo-test-billing.md#inngest-scheduling-for-vercel).
Account deletion uses a daily Inngest sweep at 02:00 UTC / 07:30 IST. Configure a stable
`DELETION_TOMBSTONE_HMAC_KEY` before enabling them. Deletion begins irreversible content cleanup on the next daily run after
a minimum 15-minute waiting period, targeting completion within 30 days, and cancellation recovery survives
User removal. See [lifecycle operations](docs/dodo-test-billing.md#lifecycle-and-deletion-operations)
for migration review, provider outages, key preservation, backup
restore fencing and rollback requirements. Automated verification uses disposable
Docker PostgreSQL and fake providers; these checks do not exercise real charges.

Before a payments launch, follow [Minimum hardening deployment and recovery](docs/minimum-hardening.md).
Keep checkout disabled through the production rollout. The runbook covers rolling limits, daily rate-limit cleanup,
Gmail provider pauses, credential key rotation, deployment checks and compatible rollback.

Operator monitoring and webhook alert delivery have been removed. After stopping
old workers, apply `20261021000000_remove_operator_alerts` to drop the unused alert
outbox and deletion-alert bookkeeping; financial, delivery and deletion-recovery
records remain. Synchronize Inngest and verify `minimum-hardening-monitor` and
`operator-alert-delivery` are absent. The replacement `rate-limit-cleanup` runs
daily at 04:00 UTC / 09:30 IST (`0 4 * * *`). It deletes up to 10,000 stale limiter
rows in batches of 500, skipping locked rows. Rows qualify only when `cleanupAt`
is more than one day old. Rate limits expire during requests independently of
cleanup. The idle cleanup costs two executions/day (about 60 per 30 days).
Automatic operator notifications and the minute heartbeat are no longer provided;
review safe logs and persisted recovery state manually.

Deletion credentials are erased when their deadline is within one day, reserving
one daily interval before the original day-30 deadline. A missed or delayed run can
still delay erasure. Daily deletion discovery prepares legacy requests and emits
only one worker event per due job. Attachment maintenance ignores deleting users,
and host billing recovery no longer independently schedules account deletion.
